podcast.body: An album track from *Music for the Masses*, this song is used to illustrate the immense complexity of ISRC numbering, having been re-released on various labels in multiple territories, remixed countless times (even Martin Gore doesn't know how many by 2003), and released across different physical and digital formats, including monthly versions with "Route 66" covers. "Take a song like, I don't know, The Pesh Modes Behind the Wheel. It's an album track from the band's 1987 Music for the Mass' album, which was released on mute records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Martin Gore of Depeche Mode once estimated that there were possibly 80 or more remixes for this song. These included various distinct mixes such as the "Mega Mix," "Mega Dub," "Extended Remix," "Beatmaster's Mix," "Chef Petty Bowen Mix," "Seven-In-Tree Mix," "Caterlty Mix," and "Pritz Mix," in addition to the original album mix. Some versions were standalone, while others incorporated elements from Depeche Mode's cover of "Route 66." "I once asked Martin Gore how many remixes there were of a song like Behind the Wheel, and he just shrugged and said, I don't know, 80 maybe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song from the album "Music for the Masses" has been remixed so many times, both legally and illegally, that even the band members themselves do not know the exact number of versions that exist. "There have been so many remixes of behind the wheel from music for the masses, both of the legal and illegal variety that no one, no one in the Peshmo knows exactly how many there are."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was released as a single from the "Music for the Masses" album and quickly became a global hit, marking a pivotal moment in Depeche Mode's career. "Singles from that record, Strange Love, Never Let Me Down Again, and Behind the Wheel, were global hits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
